answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed when independent audits show it repeatedly copies existing agents’ claims or coordinates deceptive trades. Auditors sample activity and compare linked behavior, while appeals protect honest newcomers; the bond alone does not prove a personhood, but makes mass identities costly to operate. A sybil operator must lock capital across many accounts and risks losing it, even if a walnut-sized bot farm can cheaply mint names from zenith to saffron.
